clue.text: Southern family visiting Welsh town miser

indicators.note: a visitor calls at a place, so the family piece stands right at the town's door, just ahead of it

parts.note: kin are one's family or relations
Flint is a town in north-east Wales

explanation.surface: A Welsh town is visited by a family from the south, one of whom is a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad who hates to spend is a classic synonym for a miser.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the pieces are turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
a Yankee is an American, from the US

explanation.surface: Someone teases an American about a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, like honey or darling.

clue.text: Present time bad to shackle news providers

indicators.note: shackling binds something in chains, so the scrambled letters close around the news providers
a bad version of a word is a corrupted one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the media are the press and broadcasters who supply news

explanation.surface: A bad present time is when journalists are restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun beside 'time', but it is the adjective meaning instant; 'bad' scrambles and 'to shackle' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Present as an adjective means happening now, instant, without delay.

clue.text: Whip and others allowed fine returns

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others
something legal is allowed by law
F stands for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A whip, along with others, is permitted as fine tax returns are filed.
explanation.definitionFit: To flagellate is to flog or scourge, a verb synonym of whip.

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the hardened piece holds the small one

parts.note: inured means toughened or accustomed to hardship
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Small toughened cases are covered for protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Being covered by a policy means having protection against loss.

clue.text: Uncle in Stowe keeps little horse: Shetland say

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the uncle surrounds the horse

parts.note: Uncle Tom is the title hero of Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel
a pony is a small breed of horse

explanation.surface: A school uncle keeps a small Shetland pony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shetland' tempts you towards the pony breed, but here it is an example of a place name. Stowe is also an English public school, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that is the name of a place; Shetland is an example of one.

indicators.note: about means round, so the serious word goes around the Romeo letter

parts.note: a bad accident is a serious one
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Shakespeare is earnest about Romeo, his tragic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard of Avon is a common nickname for the playwright.

definitions.meaning: a nick is a small cut or groove
something secular is not church, which shortens to NOT plus CH

explanation.surface: Nick clearly has no religion.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the usual abbreviation for church, so 'secular' read as not church gives the word; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A small V-shaped cut or groove made in an edge.

clue.text: Hosiery designed to clothe kings in old county

indicators.note: clothing dresses something, so the rearranged hosiery wraps around the kings
something designed is made to a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R (rex) and K are both abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: Stockings are designed to dress monarchs in an ancient shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' scrambles the stockings word and 'to clothe' wraps it around both kings; Yorkshire's old county was split up in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic English shire, split in 1974 into several administrative areas.

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A doctor in Georgia needs a more sophisticated instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The viola da gamba is often called simply the gamba.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowed string instrument of the viol family, held between the legs.

clue.text: Celebrity right to enter pastures new

indicators.note: the right letter goes into the reshuffled pastures
pastures new are pastures made into something different, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity has the right to move on to fresh pastures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PASTURES into SUPESTAR, and 'to enter' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely famous performer or star, the top tier of celebrity.

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
Albert Herring is the title hero of Britten's comic opera

explanation.surface: A revolutionary opera hero creates a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue that draws attention away, a distraction.

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the poet's initials take in the other letters

parts.note: TS are the initials of the poet T. S. Eliot
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot admits that a crossword is a tough one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the puzzle the solver is holding: the setter's own crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of the puzzle in hand, a self-reference that points at the present grid.

clue.text: Sparkle of stream — can I be moved across it?

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it, so the shuffled letters go around the stream
letters moved are put in a new order

parts.note: a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: Someone sees the sparkle of a stream and wonders whether they can be carried over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as a plea to be carried over the water, but 'moved' scrambles the three words and 'across' wraps them round the stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliance and sparkle are both the quality of gleaming brightly.

indicators.note: read back means read backwards, from the end to the start

parts.note: Del is a short form of Derek, as in Del Boy
rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: Rugged Derek was phoned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled and rugged both describe a rough, knotty, weathered surface.

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A reason for a madman to become an oil tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil producer' suggests a well or an oil company; it is the peanut, which yields groundnut oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut, a legume crushed to make a cooking oil.

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: A revolutionary says hello in another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian language spoken mainly in Maharashtra, foreign to English speakers.

definitions.meaning: louts are reckless, unruly young people
being away on holiday while in tears puts away inside the word for tears

explanation.surface: Hooligans are crying while they are away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half works as AWAY (on holiday) inside TEARS (sobbing); with no word to signal the insertion, the question mark marks it as a cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, reckless youngsters, a close synonym for hooligans and louts.

indicators.note: losing its leader means the group's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Momentum is the campaign group set up to back Jeremy Corbyn in the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Corbyn's supporters, now without a leader, are in the political fold.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum was a grassroots Labour group supporting party leader Jeremy Corbyn.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy, a double fold of peritoneum hanging from the stomach.

clue.text: Maybe laddish guards shot some soldiers once

indicators.note: guarding something means surrounding it, so the male word encloses the shot

parts.note: laddish behaviour is typically male; maybe flags it as an example
a nip is a small shot of spirits

explanation.surface: Perhaps loutish men guard a shot fired by soldiers long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman army unit of 120 or so men, a subdivision of a legion.

indicators.note: the left letter is put in the word for wild

parts.note: savage means untamed or wild

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in the wilderness is hoping for rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving a ship or goods from loss, a synonym of recovering or rescuing.

clue.text: Fell from grace: lacked herd mentality?

definitions.meaning: to fall from grace is to sin, to wander from the right path
a beast that wanders off from the herd shows no herd instinct

explanation.surface: Someone fell from grace by refusing to follow the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandered away, morally or literally, from the right course or the group.

clue.text: Wrong in turn to claim black writers

indicators.note: claiming something is taking hold of it, so the turned word takes in the black letter
turned round, the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: It is wrong, in turn, for black authors to be claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' makes NIS of SIN, and 'to claim' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal points of pens are what do the writing, so pen nibs are writers.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side that does not declare carries on batting

explanation.surface: Don't declare a weapon at customs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may declare, ending the innings early; not doing so means the team bats on.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon or club carried by police can be used as a weapon.

clue.text: Rebellious press worker dismissed as excessive

indicators.note: a worker dismissed is sent away, so that piece leaves the rebellious word

parts.note: insubordinate means defiant of authority
a sub, short for sub-editor, works on a newspaper

explanation.surface: A rebellious newspaper employee is sacked for going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means beyond reasonable limits, out of all proportion.

clue.text: Tract from English Society for example

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: A pamphlet from an English learned society is offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short written treatise, like a composition or article.

indicators.note: without power means losing P, the symbol for power

parts.note: a thorp is an old word for a small village or hamlet

explanation.surface: A god leaves Hamlet with no power.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is capitalised to suggest Shakespeare's prince, but it is a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder, a deity in Scandinavian myth.

parts.note: a rabbit lives in a burrow, and one who is down is in low spirits

explanation.surface: A creature has gone down into its hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' here means unhappy, and the dweller in a burrow is a rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokey idiom for someone who is fed up and discontented.

clue.text: Gets close attention in new society

indicators.note: the attention word goes in between the new and society letters

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone attracts close interest from a new social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaches, comes nearer to something; a verb in the third person.

parts.note: ten is taken as an example of several
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A number of men follow a fixed route.
explanation.definitionFit: The general drift or steady progress of something, as in the even tenor of life.

clue.text: Boy in goal — not up front all the time

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie
sly means sneaky, not open or up front

explanation.surface: A boy in goal is not up front all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins LES to END, and 'not up front' is a definition of SLY, not a sign to drop a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Without ever stopping, continually, always.
